tag: Schools, workplaces & study — always in use

vocab.example: The first few months were a steep learning curve, to be honest.
I really value the hands-on experience I get, not just theory.

vocab.meaning: manage several tasks due at the same time
vocab.example: During busy periods I'm constantly having to juggle multiple deadlines.
I did burn out a bit towards the end of last term, if I'm honest.

vocab.meaning: the balance between job/study and personal life
vocab.example: The work-life balance isn't always great during busy periods.
Some of it can get pretty monotonous, if I'm honest.

vocab.meaning: a large amount of work to complete
vocab.example: We've got a heavy workload around exam time, generally.

vocab.term: pay off in the long run
vocab.example: It's hard now, but I think it'll pay off in the long run.

bandTip: 🎯 Lexical Resource: notice the same toolkit of collocations (juggle multiple deadlines, burn out, monotonous) works whether you're a pupil, a student, or a working professional — Band 8+ isn't about having separate vocabulary for every scenario, it's applying a strong core vocabulary flexibly to whatever question you're actually asked.

questions.text: Are you a student? What school do you go to?
questions.model: Yeah, I'm still at school, actually, in my final year at a fairly average-sized secondary school in my city.

questions.text: What's your favourite subject at school?
questions.model: Probably maths, if I'm honest, mainly because I find it satisfying once things click, even though it was a steep learning curve at first.

questions.text: Do you like your school?
questions.model: I do, generally, yeah — the teachers are pretty supportive, though we've got a heavy workload around exam time.

questions.text: What do you dislike about school?
questions.model: Probably just how monotonous some of the lessons can feel, if I'm honest, especially subjects I'm not that into.

questions.text: What do you want to do after you finish school?
questions.model: I'm planning to go to university, actually, to study something science-related, though I haven't fully decided on the subject yet.

questions.text: Are you a student? What are you studying?
questions.model: Yes, I'm currently at university, studying business, in my second year now.

questions.text: Why did you choose to study that subject?
questions.model: Honestly, it felt like a fairly practical choice, something that would keep a lot of career options open rather than narrowing things down too early.

questions.text: What do you like about your course?
questions.model: I'd say the hands-on experience through group projects, mainly — it's a lot less monotonous than just sitting through lectures all day.

questions.text: Is there anything you dislike about your studies?
questions.model: If I'm honest, it's having to juggle multiple deadlines around exam season — I did burn out a bit last term, to be truthful.

questions.text: What do you plan to do after you graduate?
questions.model: I'm not entirely sure yet, though I'd like to get some hands-on experience in industry first — hopefully it'll pay off in the long run.

questions.text: Do you work? What do you do?
questions.model: I do, yeah — I work in marketing, for a mid-sized company back in my hometown.

questions.text: Why did you choose that job?
questions.model: Mostly because it let me be creative day to day, if I'm honest, rather than being stuck doing the same repetitive tasks.

questions.text: What do you like about your job?
questions.model: Probably the variety, really — no two days are quite the same, which keeps it from ever feeling too monotonous.

questions.text: Is there anything you dislike about your job?
questions.model: If I'm honest, having to juggle multiple deadlines at once sometimes — the work-life balance isn't always great during busy periods.

questions.text: Do you think you'll stay in this job for a long time?
questions.model: For now, yes, probably — though I wouldn't rule out trying to climb the career ladder somewhere else eventually.

vocab.example: It's a stone's throw from the coast, actually.
It's turned into a sprawling suburb over the last decade.

vocab.meaning: a tightly connected group of people who know each other well
vocab.example: What I like most is that close-knit community feel.

vocab.meaning: a place seen as dull or unimportant
vocab.example: My grandparents live in a fairly quiet backwater, to be honest.
The town centre has undergone significant changes since I was a kid.

vocab.meaning: to have spent one's whole early life in a place
vocab.example: I was born and raised there, more or less.
It's known for its picturesque scenery, especially the riverside.
It's honestly a far cry from how I remember it as a kid.

bandTip: 🎯 Coherence: every answer here directly answers the specific question asked (size, duration, change, comparison) rather than reusing one generic hometown description — examiners notice immediately when a candidate gives the same rehearsed paragraph regardless of the actual question.

questions.text: Please describe your hometown a little.
questions.model: Sure — it's a fairly small city, a stone's throw from the coast actually, and I was born and raised there, more or less.

questions.text: What is your hometown well-known for?
questions.model: Probably its picturesque scenery, if I'm honest, especially the riverside area, which draws a fair number of visitors.

questions.text: Do you like your hometown?
questions.model: I do, generally, yeah — I'd say what I like most is that close-knit community feel, everyone kind of knows everyone.

questions.text: Is that a big city or a small place?
questions.model: It's fairly small, actually, more of a large town than a proper city, if I'm honest.

questions.text: How long have you been living there?
questions.model: My whole life, pretty much, aside from a couple of years away for university.

questions.text: Do you think you will continue living there for a long time?
questions.model: Probably not forever, if I'm honest, though I'm not in any rush to leave either.

questions.text: Would you like to live in the countryside in the future?
questions.model: Actually, yes, I think I would eventually — somewhere with a bit more picturesque scenery and a lot less noise.

questions.text: Have you ever lived in the countryside?
questions.model: Not really, no — the closest I've come is visiting my grandparents, who live in a fairly quiet backwater, to be honest.

questions.text: Do you ever spend time in the countryside?
questions.model: Occasionally, yeah, mostly visiting family — it's honestly a nice break from city life.

questions.text: What is the difference between living in the countryside and the city?
questions.model: I'd say pace, mainly — the countryside's obviously a lot slower, whereas the city's constantly changing, always something new going on.

questions.text: What do people living in the countryside like to do?
questions.model: From what I've seen, a lot of outdoor stuff, gardening, walking, that sort of thing — much more than people tend to do in the city.

questions.text: What do you like to do in the countryside?
questions.model: Mostly just relax, honestly, go for long walks, completely unplug from everything for a few days.

questions.text: How has your town changed over the last 20 years?
questions.model: Quite a lot, actually — it's undergone significant changes, what used to be farmland is basically a sprawling suburb now, a far cry from how I remember it as a kid.

vocab.example: It's not huge, but it feels fairly spacious for a two-bedroom flat.
It's got a cosy feel, especially in winter.
We moved into a fully furnished flat, which made things a lot easier.
The living room gets loads of natural light in the mornings.

vocab.meaning: a layout with few or no dividing walls
vocab.example: The kitchen and living room are open-plan, which I really like.
We might downsize once the kids move out.

vocab.meaning: a party celebrating a new home
vocab.example: We had a housewarming not long after we moved in.

vocab.meaning: personalize a space so it feels comfortable and familiar
vocab.example: Small changes like that really help make it feel like home.

bandTip: 🎯 Grammatical Range: notice short, natural contrast structures like "it's not huge, but it feels fairly spacious" — a simple "not X, but Y" pattern adds nuance to a Part 1 answer without needing complex grammar.

questions.text: Can you describe the place where you live?
questions.model: Sure — it's a fairly spacious two-bedroom flat, on the third floor of a fairly modern building.

questions.text: What kind of housing accommodation do you live in?
questions.model: I live in a flat, actually, fully furnished when we first moved in, which honestly made things a lot easier.

questions.text: What do you like about your flat?
questions.model: Probably the natural light, if I'm honest — the living room faces east, so it's really bright in the mornings.

questions.text: Which room does your family spend most of the time in?
questions.model: Definitely the living room, mainly because it's open-plan with the kitchen, so everyone naturally ends up there.

questions.text: What can you see from the windows where you live?
questions.model: Mostly rooftops and a bit of a park in the distance, nothing too exciting, if I'm honest.

questions.text: Do you prefer living in a house or a flat?
questions.model: A flat, personally, mainly for practical reasons — less maintenance, and it's got a cosy feel despite being fairly small.

questions.text: What would you like to change in your flat?
questions.model: Probably the kitchen, if I could — I'd love a proper open-plan layout eventually, small changes like that really help make it feel like home.

questions.text: What do you dislike about your flat?
questions.model: Honestly, just the lack of storage — it's spacious enough day to day, but storage is definitely lacking.

questions.text: Who do you live with?
questions.model: Just my partner at the moment — it's a fairly small place, so there's no need to downsize any further, if anything we'd like a bit more room eventually.

questions.text: How long have you lived there?
questions.model: About three years now — we had a housewarming when we first moved in, actually, which feels like ages ago now.
